output.methodChoice: EDF-1 standard analysis; collected X3 and X2 (2 of 2 items)
output.brief: The field failures look real and are coming from Pellacott's 2026-built VA-220 valves, not from installers or firmware. Teardowns show internal seat leaks with a deformed slide seal. Helium retests of never-installed warehouse stock leak at 11% for 2026 Pellacott lots, versus 1% for 2025 and 0% for Durrant-Hale. Claim rates are flat across legacy and new installers and across firmware 4.1 and 4.2. The certificates are doubtful: the calibration site visit found the main leak-test rig out of service since January, no VA-220 test program on the other rigs, and certificate tables that repeat the same few sequences. So the high SupplierPath score is not reliable evidence of good valves. How sure I am: fairly confident on the defect and the paper-test problem; less sure of the seal as the cause, since seal compound was not analysed and the Corlin switch is tangled with the move to Line 3. Next: quarantine all 2026 Pellacott VA-220 stock, including the six held lots, and suspend its dock-to-stock status. Do not release the held lots on new certificates. Release only after Brenmoor's own helium testing. Do not charge back installers. Fix the scoring so records earn credit only when backed by rig logs or witnessed tests. Check other suppliers' records. Hold any seal-source change until it is tested.
